value: catalytic decomposition (cracking) of methane, CH4 -> C + 2H2, over supported Ni (also Co, Fe or carbon) catalysts, producing CO/CO2-free hydrogen and solid filamentous carbon; the catalyst is regenerated by steam gasification or air oxidation of the carbon. Continuous operation needs twin fluidised beds (cracking and regeneration)

note: 'methane cracking is not used on an industrial scale for producing hydrogen since it is not economically competitive'. The HYPRO process (1966) was a commercial circulating-fluidised-bed cracker at up to 980 degC and atmospheric pressure, producing 90% H2 on 7% Ni/Al2O3; its operating cost was high.

REACTION ENTHALPY per mole of H2 (dH298 = +74.8 kJ/mol CH4), not a measured plant energy use; steam reforming needs 63.3 kJ/mol H2 on the same basis. 37.4 kJ/mol H2 = 18.6 GJ per tonne H2. The heat can be covered by burning about 15-20% of the hydrogen produced (p.2905, ref [16]).
HYPRO fluidised-bed catalytic cracker, 'operating at temperatures up to 980 degC'. Uncatalysed thermal cracking needs >1200 degC for a reasonable yield.
